sections.h2: Which Wake County office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
Tax Administration is the department that sets values and collects payment. Reach its help desk at 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov.

One bill can hold several charges. A local agreement has the county collect for the towns and special districts inside its borders too, and the county points residents to their town hall for questions about a town's rate.

If a lender pays from escrow, no bill is mailed; check the amount online. A seller in that group should still know the actual figure.

sections.h2: What rate did Wake County set for Fiscal Year 2027?
sections.html:
The county's bill page says commissioners adopted a $2.28 billion budget on June 1 for Fiscal Year 2027 and that a 2-cent increase lifts the county rate to 53.71 cents. That covers the county share only.

Town and district rates come on top. The page offers its own illustration, a $90 increase for the owner of a $450,000 home. For your parcel, ask Tax Administration.

sections.h2: How late can you pay a Wake County tax bill?
sections.html:
January 5 is the last no-interest day, according to the county, though bills are due September 1. State law adds 2 percent from January 6, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or part month from February 1.

The county is flexible before that date. Pay in pieces of any size, no approval needed, provided the balance clears by January 5; each payment brings a statement of what remains. Short-term plans exist too, and earlier calls get better options. After a bill turns overdue, the office says it cannot help.

State law allows collection from wages, accounts or rent.

  • Pay online by bank draft, digital wallet or card.
  • Escrow accounts: the lender pays and no bill arrives.
  • Questions about a bill: 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov.

sections.h2: Which value does the bill due in September 2027 use?
sections.html:
The bill due September 1, 2027 uses values as of January 1, 2027, and rates approved by elected officials in June 2027, according to the county's revaluation FAQ. The bill due September 1, 2026 rests on January 1, 2024 values and the rates approved in June 2026.

The FAQ describes a tax bill as two numbers multiplied together: assessed value and the rate per $100 set by county and municipal officials. It prints its own worked example for a house assessed at $450,000 at the 53.71 cent county rate, and it notes that revaluation itself changes values, not rates.

State law also makes local governments publish a revenue-neutral rate during the budget process, meaning the rate that would bring in about the same revenue as before the revaluation. Officials are not required to adopt that rate.

sections.h2: How often will Wake County revalue after 2027?
sections.html:
Every two years. The commissioners voted in March 2025 to phase in a two-year cycle, with the first two-year revaluation effective January 1, 2029. The county's reason is that long gaps let increases pile up and land on owners as one sudden jump.

The FAQ adds that 37 counties, Wake among them, have revaluations effective January 1, 2027. A rulebook called the Schedule of Values, approved by the commissioners, sets the rates and ranges used to value property between revaluations, and the county posts the PDF at wake.gov/sov.

  • Look up your current assessed value at wake.gov/realestate.
  • Report wrong property data at wake.gov/rehelp, with your address or account number and any documents.
  • Expect occasional appraiser visits: badges, county-marked vehicles, usually 15 to 30 minutes, and photos of the exterior.

sections.h2: Where is Wake County Tax Administration and how do you contact it?
sections.html:
The department lists a physical location at 301 S. McDowell St., Ste. 3800, Raleigh, NC 27601, and a mailing address of P.O. Box 2331, Raleigh, NC 27602. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding county holidays.

  • Property tax: 919-856-5400. Fax: 919-856-7128.
  • Gross receipts: 919-856-5999.
  • Online help center and chat: taxhelp.wake.gov/hc, or taxhelp@wake.gov.
  • Revaluation and appraisers: 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

The county also publishes residential sales through a Residential Sales Search tool that can filter by distance, sale date, heated area and year built, and says a comparable sales tool is due in January 2027. A seller preparing for a buyer or an appeal can use these listings to see what nearby houses sold for.

sections.h2: What does the 2027 revaluation change for a Wake County seller?
sections.html:
Values reset January 1, 2027, replacing the January 1, 2024 set, and the county says later resets follow every two years. Buyers in 2027 will be pricing the tax on the new number.

The aim, per the county, is for each assessed value to match fair market value, the most probable open-market price. Work runs through neighborhooding, pricing from sales, field and office review, then notices and appeals. About 460,000 parcels fall into 5,400 neighborhoods.

  • Results go to the commissioners on January 19, 2027, and notices follow that week.
  • The county's planned appeal deadline is April 30, 2027.

These are published targets. Confirm them at 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

sections.h2: Where does a Wake County value appeal go?
sections.html:
To the county's Board of Equalization and Review. Notices of value go out first, and the revaluation page says owners can then appeal informally.

Statute sets its first meeting between the first Mondays of April and May, and a hearing request must arrive before adjournment. Beyond the board lies the state Property Tax Commission, with 30 days from the mailed decision to file. Revaluation-year boards finish by December 1.

Gather nearby sales and repair estimates first. If the appeal will outlast closing, ask your attorney about handling a later change.

sections.h2: Who can get tax relief in Wake County?
sections.html:
The county lists three state programs: Senior and Disabled, Tax Deferment and Disabled Veteran. Eligible groups are low-income owners 65 or older, low-income owners who are 100 percent disabled, and veterans with total, permanent service-connected disability or their unmarried surviving spouses.

The state sets the dollar terms: a 2026 income limit of $38,800 on the state form, a $45,000 disabled veteran exclusion, and a circuit breaker that defers part of the bill as a lien. Pick the program that fits, since an owner may use only one.

The deadline is June 1. For 2026 the county said it would consider late applications for good cause through December 31, 2026, citing illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment or delayed disability certification. Forgetting is not accepted.

sections.h2: What if you sell a Wake County house owing tax?
sections.html:
The debt stays with the parcel. State law attaches the lien as of the listing date for the tax year, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure action.

At closing, the attorney gets the amount due from Tax Administration and pays it from your proceeds. Interest starts January 6, so settle before then if you can.

With an inherited house in arrears, call Tax Administration first and ask what options remain.

faqs.q: Until when can I pay Wake County tax interest-free?
faqs.a: January 5, 2027 for the 2026 bills, per the county; interest begins the next day.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Wake County bill in pieces?
faqs.a: Yes, in any amount, without approval, as long as the bill is paid by January 5. Short-term plans are available to early callers.

faqs.q: What is the next Wake County revaluation date?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027, after the January 1, 2024 cycle, with later ones every two years.

faqs.q: Who answers Wake County tax questions?
faqs.a: Tax Administration, 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov; for revaluation, 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

faqs.q: Do older or disabled Wake owners get relief?
faqs.a: Yes: Senior and Disabled, Tax Deferment and Disabled Veteran. The deadline is June 1.
